title: Runtime slab allocator and attention dialer for elastic sequence grouping
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Heavy padding from tail-heavy request distributions increases per-token cost and reduces kernel efficiency. Current bucketing is coarse (fixed bins) and applies global padding heuristics that miss transient bursts and mixed-length workloads. Goals: (1) Reduce padding overhead by dynamically grouping concurrent requests into contiguous 'slabs' of similar sequence-length percentiles, (2) Select attention kernels per-slab using a cost model (fused MHA vs. chunked causal kernel vs. block-sparse) to minimize latency and GPU time, and (3) Coordinate small prefill warmups and decode scheduling to improve KV cache hit-rate for hot slabs without harming tail latency. Success metrics: >=15% token-cost reduction on mixed workloads, no more than 5% regression in 95th-pct latency, and clear single-digit percent latency benefit on short-seq cohorts.
acceptance_criteria: Impl runs as an opt-in runtime flag: slab_allocator.enabled=true
Per-slab kernel selection exercised and logged (kernel_hint in request traces)
Bench: median token-cost reduction >= 15% on benchmark suite (chatty/mixed/long-tail)
Perf dashboards showing no >5% regression in 95th-pct latency after rollout
Smoke tests for streaming and function-calling preserved
notes: Design: slab allocator builds a histogram of incoming seqlens over 100ms sliding windows, then emits contiguous percentile ranges (slabs) sized by token footprint budget (configurable). Slabs are mutable and decay over 1s to adapt to bursts.
Kernel cost model: offline-calibrated cost matrix for kernels by (seq_len, batch_size, kv_cache_usage); runtime estimator picks kernel and emits kernel_hint for tracing and fallback.

Attention dialer: small decision engine that prefers fused MHA for dense short slabs, causal chunked kernel for mid-length slabs where memory bandwidth dominates, and block-sparse for long sequences when sparsity ratio > 0.6.

Padding reduction: intra-slab slot packing packs short requests into leftover slots of larger-seq requests when latency SLO allows (latency budget gating). Tail-splitting splits very long requests into prefix prefill + fragment decode to avoid dragging slab bucket limits.
Prefill/decode scheduling: schedule a light-weight prefill for top-K hot slabs to warm KV; decode tokens for low-latency cohorts get prioritized token slots in each GPU microstep.

Trade-offs considered: stricter slabs reduce padding more but increase scheduling jitter and potential starvation; decision engine includes latency budget check to prevent negative impact on 95th-pct latency.

Benchmarks so far (prototype A100-40GB): mixed-chat benchmark shows ~18% token-cost reduction, 22% throughput improvement for medium-batch runs; occasional +3% 95th latency on pathological adversarial bursts (mitigated by gating).

implementation_steps: 1) Finalize slab histogram module and edge-cases (empty window, burst decay)
2) Implement kernel cost model interface and safe fallback path
3) Integrate slab_id + kernel_hint into tracing/span headers
4) Add slot-packing allocator with latency gating hook
5) Implement lightweight prefill warmups with per-slab budget and memory cap
7) Run perf suite on canary cluster, iterate on decay/window and gate thresholds
8) Rollout plan: gated -> internal canary -> 10% hosted -> 50% hosted -> global disable/rollback if p95 regressions >5%
